account.note: THIS RUN STOPPED AT THE STALENESS GUARD AND PUBLISHED NOTHING. THE DAILY ENTRY MANDATE IS UNDISCHARGED FOR 2026-08-11. The open slot fired at 13:40 ET against an 09:33 ET slot: 247 minutes late, four hours and seven minutes, against a guard of 25 minutes in either direction. WHY THE MANDATE LOSES TO THE GUARD, WHICH IS THE ONE DECISION ON THIS RUN WORTH DEFENDING. The mandate says standing aside is not available to this slot, and the guard says a run this far outside its window publishes nothing. The guard wins by its own terms, and the reason is not procedural: an entry struck at 13:40 is not the open's entry carrying a late timestamp. It is a mid-session entry written by the one slot with a standing licence to open positions, on a tape four hours removed from the reasoning behind it, and it would enter the record labelled 'open' and corrupt the exact comparison the mandate was created to produce. A forced entry is a compromised thesis, honestly labelled. A stale entry is a compromised timestamp, and this board has no label for that. So 2026-08-11 has no specification and the run row carries the reason. FIVE SCHEDULED SLOTS PRODUCED NO ROW AT ALL BEFORE 13:40. The 09:33 open and the 10:17, 11:17, 12:17 and 13:17 hourlies each wrote nothing - not a decline, not a failed connection, no evidence they fired. That is the desktop-scheduler failure mode already described in the scheduler note, escalated rather than diagnosed from here, and it is a larger fact about today than anything on the tape. WHAT THE GUARD DID NOT COST IS AN EXIT, AND THAT IS A FACT ABOUT TODAY RATHER THAN A DEFENCE OF ARRIVING LATE. Exits were checked before anything else and all four levels on the one open position are clear: OKLO, 2 shares at a 45.1499 average against a live 46.53 bid, +3.06%, 2.76 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost, a 54.18 target that needs the bid up 16.44%, a 41.54 stop that needs it down 10.72%, and the 8/14 close as the time stop with today session two of five. An open position went from Friday's 16:33 retro to 13:40 today with no run looking at it. Had a level been through in that window it would have gone four hours unenforced, and nothing about this run's diligence would have changed that. NO OPTION IS HELD, so no no-fly window closes anything: the option position list was queried live and is empty, stated rather than assumed. NO EARNINGS ON THE UNDERLYING - the calendar was pulled live at 760 events across 8/11 to 8/15, OKLO in none of them, SMCI on 8/11 pm verified at an 0.88 estimate still the only watched name inside the window. No straddle was owed on the position and none is claimed. THE PRE-CLOSE NAMED A RISK THAT DID NOT ARRIVE, AND NOBODY GETS CREDIT FOR IT. Friday's close wrote down that OKLO had fallen 7.44% in a session and that another move of that size lands at 41.49, through the 41.54 stop, then held anyway on the rulebook's ground that a position closes at a level and not at a forecast. The session went the other way: 44.49 settled close to 46.53, +4.59%, and the stop is now 10.72% away, wider than at any read yesterday. Writing the danger down in advance was correct AND the direction it resolved in was forecast by nobody. Those are two separate findings, and the run that named the downside has no more claim on this outcome than one that had named the upside would have. BREADTH INVERTED AND THE LEADERSHIP INVERTED WITH IT: 4 green, 1 flat, 7 red against 10 red of 12 on Friday, and the two names leading today are the two that led the decline - SMR best at +4.90% and OKLO second at +4.59%, both nuclear, after finishing 8/10 fourth-worst and worst respectively. JOBY is the worst name on the board at -5.45% having closed Friday as the best. THE 8/10 OFFICIAL CLOSE IS NOW PUBLISHED AT 44.49, the regular-session figure the retro named as its alternative rather than the 44.20 extended-hours mark it used; the retro's own stated alternative total of 1008.56 is the one the settled data supports. Left for the bench and perf rows to correct rather than edited here. ORDER RECORD QUERIED DIRECTLY AND NOW CARRIED INTO A SECOND SESSION: exactly one order exists in this account since 8/7, the OKLO buy filled 10:39:30 ET on 8/10 at 45.1499 against a 45.40 limit, placed_agent agentic, with no specification from any run here behind it. The escalation stands open, unanswered and uncompounded. Deployable is 919.58 settled with nothing pending and no pending deposits. CONCURRENCY, RECORDED BECAUSE IT AFFECTED THIS FILE: the 13:17 hourly fired in the same minute as this run and wrote a position-only sync here at 13:43:52 on a 46.54 bid while this run held a 46.53 read struck at 17:41:23 UTC. Its note is preserved verbatim on the position below rather than overwritten; this board is struck at one timestamp across all twelve names; and the one-cent gap is two reads seconds apart rather than a disagreement about anything.
account.priorNote: THE OVERNIGHT HOLD IS THIS SLOT'S ONE JOB AND IT IS DECIDED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED. OKLO is held. 2 shares at a 45.1499 average against a 44.82 bid: -0.73%, 0.66 of unrealized loss on a 90.30 cost, a 54.18 target that needs the bid up 20.9%, a 41.54 stop that needs it down 7.3%, and the 8/14 close as the time stop with today session one of five. Four levels checked against a live bid, four clear, nothing sold, no exit specification owed. THE LEVEL THAT WOULD CHANGE THE HOLD IS 41.54. NO OPTION IS HELD, SO NO NO-FLY WINDOW CLOSES ANYTHING TODAY, and no watched name reports tonight - the calendar was re-pulled live at 934 events across 8/10 to 8/14 with OKLO in none of them. THE HOLD IS NOT FREE, AND THE ARITHMETIC BELONGS ON THIS SIDE OF THE NIGHT RATHER THAN TOMORROW'S OPEN. OKLO fell 3.60 today - 48.42 to 44.82, -7.44%, the worst name on this board for an eighth consecutive read. From 44.82 another -7.44% lands at 41.49, which is BELOW the 41.54 stop. A repeat of today gaps through the stop rather than filling at it, and the 7.3% of room the stop shows is less protection than the number looks like on a name that has just travelled 7.4% in one session. It is held anyway, and the reason is the rulebook rather than nerve: a position closes when the target, the stop or the time stop says so, not when a run forecasts the next session, and a stop widened or pre-empted by a guess is not a stop. What this run owes is that the risk is named in advance instead of discovered.
account.operatorNote: OPERATOR, 2026-08-10, answering the funding escalation carried in the notes above rather than editing either of them. The 900.00 is a deposit I made; the account is funded to about 1000 and the cash is spendable. This answers the deposit and NOTHING ELSE - it is not an authorisation for the OKLO order the 10:46 sync found, which no run here published and which arrived through the same agentic channel escalated on 8/7; that escalation stands open and unanswered. Three rule changes go with it and all three are written up in docs/RULES.md with their arithmetic, because a licence recorded without its constraints is how this record stops being worth reading. The position ceiling goes from two to four, capped at 40% in any one name and at two names in any one complex - the complex cap is the one that matters on a board whose whole universe moves together. Overnight holds are not a change: they were always allowed, the five-session time stop stands, and it is not extendable by conviction. The objective is still about 10% a day, which is roughly 101 dollars at this size and needs a fully deployed four-name book to average +10% in a session against a +20% take-profit; where the objective and the rulebook conflict, the rulebook wins and the retro records the shortfall. What the deposit does NOT do is reopen options - that refusal has been on spread for three sessions, most recently 36% of mark against a 10% ceiling, and no balance narrows a spread. The 10:22 hourly was right to escalate this rather than size against it.

positions.note: FOUR LEVELS CHECKED AGAINST A LIVE 46.53 BID, FOUR CLEAR, AND THE POSITION IS GREEN FOR THE FIRST TIME. +3.06%, 2.76 of unrealized gain on a 90.30 cost; the 54.18 target needs the bid up 16.44%, the 41.54 stop needs it down 10.72%, and the time stop is the 8/14 close with today session two of five. Nothing is sold and no exit specification is owed. NO EXIT COULD HAVE BEEN ENFORCED THIS MORNING IN ANY CASE - this run fired four hours after its slot and stopped at the staleness guard, so these levels were unwatched from Friday's 16:33 retro until 13:40 today. They happened to move the right way. That is luck, and it is recorded as luck rather than as an outcome this board managed. THE PRE-CLOSE HELD THIS AGAINST ITS OWN ARITHMETIC AND WAS RIGHT FOR THE REASON IT GAVE, WHICH IS NARROWER THAN BEING RIGHT ABOUT THE PRICE. Friday's close wrote down that a repeat of the day's -7.44% lands at 41.49, through the stop, and held anyway because a position closes at a level and not at a forecast. The name is +4.59% today. What that confirms is the rule. It says nothing about whether the gap risk was real - it was, and it simply did not happen on this occasion. A run that now describes the hold as a good read rather than a correct procedure would be learning the wrong thing from it. FROM WORST TO SECOND-BEST IN ONE SESSION. It was the worst name on this board for eight consecutive reads on 8/10 and is second only to SMR today, +4.59% against +4.90%. Both are nuclear, which is the two-per-complex cap describing itself again: the complex that led the decline is leading the recovery, together, and four names off this list would still be one position at four times the size. SIZE UNCHANGED AND STILL AT THE FLOOR: 93.06 at the bid is 9.19% of the 1012.68 account, under the ~10% threshold at which the 8/10 rule warns rather than blocks, and nearer that floor than the 40% ceiling. Carried to a full +20% take-profit it adds about 18.06, which is 1.8% of the account against an objective near 10% a day. Explicitly not an argument to add: adding to a position because it has moved in your favour is chasing, which the rulebook lists by name. Provenance unchanged after an eighth direct query and now into a second session: one order in this account since 8/7, tagged agentic, no specification from any run here behind it. Tagged nuclear, which puts SMR and LEU on the same two-name limit as this position.

entryWatch.setup: The open slot did not fire in its window - the entry mandate is unmet for 2026-08-11
entryWatch.trigger: None, and deliberately none. The staleness guard closed this slot at 13:40 ET, 247 minutes after 09:33, and it is not reopenable later in the day by this run or any other: the mid-session slots are exits-only and the pre-close may not open a position in the last thirty minutes.
entryWatch.why: THE MANDATE IS THE THING THIS RUN FAILED TO DO, AND IT IS LOGGED AS AN ENTRY ROW SO IT CANNOT BE READ AS A QUIET DAY. The mandate says standing aside is not available to this slot; the guard says a run more than 25 minutes outside its window publishes nothing; the guard wins by its own terms. What makes that the right ordering rather than a convenient one: the mandate exists to test whether trading daily beats patience, and a specification struck at 13:40 tests neither. It is not the open's entry - it is a mid-session entry written by the slot with the widest licence on this board, on a tape four hours removed from its own reasoning, and it would enter the record labelled 'open' and corrupt exactly the comparison the mandate was created to produce. A forced entry is a compromised thesis honestly labelled; a stale entry is a compromised timestamp, and there is no label for that. THE CAUSE IS UPSTREAM OF JUDGEMENT AND IT IS THE KNOWN ONE: the scheduler is a desktop task that fires only while the operator's app is open, and five slots today - the open and four hourlies - produced no row at all before 13:40.

entryWatch.trigger: None. The print is tonight, 8/11 pm, verified live against 760 events in the 8/11-8/15 window at an 0.88 estimate, and it is still the only watched name inside it. The 8/14 32-strike straddle priced a 13.7% move at Friday's close against a rulebook stop of 8%.
entryWatch.why: Unchanged, and now unreachable in time as well as on arithmetic. 31.39 bid, -0.22%, essentially flat into its own print - the five-session run of relative strength that made it the best name on this board has stopped exactly where positioning into a catalyst usually does, which is what item 5 describes. The refusal was never about direction: an 8% stop sitting inside a 13.7% implied move is an exit the event is priced to jump rather than fill, and any 3-6 week option necessarily spans the print and is forbidden outright, so the option route was never open either. THE ONE NUMBER HERE THAT IS STALE IS NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY REFRESHED: moves.json still carries the 31.70 spot and the 0.137 ratio struck together at Friday's 15:35, and the live bid is 31.39. It is deliberately not half-refreshed - re-marking spot without re-pulling the straddle at the same instant makes the implied range wrong in the flattering direction, which is the failure that file's own comment warns about. That pass belongs to the 15:33 pre-close, which is also the run that prunes this row once the print has passed.

entryWatch.setup: The speculative complex - Friday's decline unwound by the same names that led it
entryWatch.trigger: No level. 4 green, 1 flat, 7 red against 10 red of 12 at Friday's bell, with the recovery concentrated in the two nuclear names that fell hardest - SMR +4.90% and OKLO +4.59%.
entryWatch.why: THE CORRELATION FINDING HOLDS FOR A THIRD READ AND FOR THE THIRD TIME WITH THE SIGN FLIPPED. Friday produced twelve names down together at 14:22, eleven up or flat together at 15:21, and today the two hardest-hit names of that session lead a partial recovery while Friday's best name, JOBY, is today's worst at -5.45%. Co-movement persists; direction does not; and the rank ordering inverts wholesale between sessions as readily as within one. That is now a daily-scale observation rather than only an hourly one, and it is the whole ground the two-per-complex cap rests on - a cap needs to know that four names share one stop, not which way they are going. NOTHING IS PROPOSED, AND ON THIS RUN THAT IS THE GUARD RATHER THAN A READ. The mandate discharges through the open slot and the open slot is closed; the entry-watch row above carries that. Independently of the guard, this is also not the setup the rulebook buys: a one-session bounce in the two names that fell hardest is a reversal off a decline, not the day-2/3 pullback after strength, and the complex cap would allow exactly one of SMR or LEU beside the OKLO position in any case. THE DEAD JOBY SPECIFICATION IS RE-MARKED AN EIGHTH TIME AND FINALLY SAYS SOMETHING. The forced 8.85 limit expired unfilled at 10:30 on 8/10; JOBY is 8.33 bid, -5.88% against that limit and -5.45% on the day. Seven marks across Friday wandered between +2.3% and -3.4% and carried no information in either direction. The eighth is not a wander: an entry that sat five cents from its level at Friday's bell is now fifty-two cents away, and the expiry that looked like a missed fill was a bullet dodged. That is worth one line and not a thesis - it is one session, on the same board that just reversed its own rank ordering.
